### F-R18-01: filtering system enqueues breaks a content-free FIFO dequeue

**Plan location:** host binding table line 83; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001 line 205; TEST-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 line 370; UC-1 line 477; A3 line 579. **Defect:** line 83 says a system-event `enqueue` is classified and never minted, while every `dequeue` has no content and delivers the head of the bridge's queued request entries. The bridge specifies no placeholder for a skipped system enqueue and no rule for its later dequeue or removal. If a system event is ahead of a user request, its dequeue can deliver the user request without a host delivery event for that request. **Evidence:** the live Claude Code transcript `/home/sharpninja/.claude/projects/-home-sharpninja-github-McpServer--claude-worktrees-session-20261009/49428485-c8ea-46d7-86c6-58add8faed97.jsonl` has a structurally marked system-event enqueue immediately followed by a content-free dequeue at 2026-10-09T03:43:01.521Z; a read-only scan found 39 such adjacent pairs in worktree transcripts. The dequeue record has only `type`, `operation`, `timestamp`, `sessionId`. The queue contract tracks only minted requests. **To PASS:** define how all enqueue positions, including filtered system events, are represented or fail closed when a dequeue cannot be attributed; the later user request must remain queued until its own delivery. Strengthen FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC010/FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001 and TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, and add A3 RED cases for system enqueue -> user enqueue -> system dequeue -> user dequeue, removal, crash/replay, and zero wrong-turn writes. Propagate to wire, UC-1, TODO, and handoff. **Classification:** implementer requirement/contract/test edit under D1/D5/D6; no new operator decision.

### F-R18-02: C2 cannot determine the consumers required to acknowledge an alias

**Plan location:** C2 line 119; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008 line 200; TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008 AC-007 line 350; A8 line 589; P0.7 line 175; coordination gate line 115. **Defect:** the locked schema stores a mutable global `consumers: [consumerId]` and each alias's `acks`, but the pruning rule refers to consumers registered **when that alias was committed**. If consumer B registers after alias X is committed for A, then A acknowledges X, current `consumers=[A,B]` and `acks=[A]` cannot tell whether B was required at X's commit. The listed `AliasRecord` has no required-consumer snapshot or registration epoch. Conversely, a consumer needed for pre-existing pending events could register after an alias was pruned. `onAliasCommitted(handler)` also lacks a concrete handler signature and return type. MEMORY-PROCESS-007's 23:37:53Z C2 interface CONTRACT has no Codex ACK in the 15-memory read; the plan's generic line 115 says amendments need ACK before dependent integration, but A8 names only the prior C3 ACK as a precondition. **To PASS:** lock the per-alias required-consumer set or an equivalent durable registration-epoch rule, define registration before relevant mint/outbox use and unregistered-consumer behavior, complete the callback signature, and name A8/QB contract tests for late registration, crash/restart, partial ack, and pruning. Make C2 peer ACK an explicit A8 integration gate and update the TODO technicalDetails/handoff after the ACK. **Classification:** implementer plan/requirement/test edit plus the already prescribed Codex peer CONTRACT/ACK; no operator decision unless that exchange raises a new product choice.
